_comment: Per-program display configuration (plain JSON in the repo, decision records 0007 and 0013 to 0015). Versions are date-ranged and chosen by the OFFENCE date. The DEFAULT block is used for any notice whose program is not configured or cannot be matched; a program's own switch always wins, and a switch a program does not set is inherited from the default block. Modes: on, off, not_applicable, not_yet.

details.label: Seconds after the light turned red

explainer.heading: Sensors in the road
explainer.body: Piezoelectric sensors embedded at the stop line detect when a vehicle crosses after the light turns red. A second sensor confirms the vehicle continued through.

explainer.heading: Checked before every session
explainer.body: The operator checks the camera before every session. That check is recorded, and a reading is only used if it was done.

link.text: See the check for this session

explainer.heading: Two photographs
explainer.body: The camera takes two photos — one as the vehicle crosses the stop line and one as it moves through the intersection — recording position, speed and time since the light changed.

messages.text: Running a red light at this stage is extremely dangerous. At three seconds or more after the light changed, crossing traffic may already be moving through the intersection.
The light had been red for more than a second before entry. Other road users may have begun to move into the intersection.

explainer.heading: Calibrated sensors
explainer.body: The camera system records vehicle speed using calibrated sensors and photographs the vehicle at the time of the offence.

explainer.heading: Checked before every session
explainer.body: The operator checks the camera before every session. That check is recorded, and a reading is only used if it was done.

explainer.heading: A person is there
explainer.body: An operator sets up and runs the camera, and can be asked about what they did.

messages.text: At speeds above 30 km/h the risk of serious injury in a collision rises sharply, for both vehicle occupants and anyone outside the vehicle.
Travelling more than 10 km/h over the limit significantly increases stopping distance and the severity of any impact.
